messages:
ajay: Heads-up — saw a KV cache memory spiral on host gpu-pool-7 while running long-chat workloads. resident_bytes keeps growing even after client disconnects. Anyone seen this pattern?
maria: Yep, noticed something similar yesterday in perf tests for long_context_v2. Appears to be fragment + stale-residency behaviour.
devon: Do you have quick numbers? tail of long contexts or kv evictions?
ajay: Quick dump from the profiler: 
```
kv_resident_bytes: 12.3GB -> 18.7GB over 2h
kv_evictions_total: 120 (mostly tenant X)
kv_reuse_hits: 0.2% (for tails > 8k tokens)
long_context_tail_count: 2.1k
```
ajs: (typo) meant ajay ^^
maria: That reuse_hits number screams fragmentation and low reuse due to unique prefixes. Could be noisy neighbor that pins pages.
sasha: What eviction policy are we using on that pool? LRU across tenants or per-tenant?
ajay: Current impl is global LRU with per-tenant soft limits but they are enforced by eviction only when pool-wide resident>threshold. So a tenant can hog residency until threshold.
maria: There's also a bug in compaction path where freed blocks smaller than 256B aren't merged which creates fragmentation over long sequences. We saw that in the allocator trace.
devon: Proposed quick mitigation: implement time-based soft TTL for per-tenant KV residency. If a prefix hasn't been used for X minutes, mark as reclaimable with lower priority eviction. That + per-tenant hard cap should limit noisy neighbor.
sasha: +1. Also we can score entries with a small hotness metric: hotness = recent_hits / (1 + resident_bytes). Evict lowest hotness first but factor tenant fairness by boosting score of underutilized tenants.
ajay: Example pseudo: 
```
score = recent_hits / (1 + resident_bytes)
adjusted = score * fairness_boost(tenant_id)
evict lowest adjusted
```
maria: fairness_boost could be derived from tenant_weight = min(1, baseline_bytes / tenant_resident_bytes) to prefer evicting from oversized tenants.
devon: We should also surface metrics: per-tenant resident_bytes, per-tenant kv_hits, tail_context_fraction. Current dashboards only show pool-wide numbers.
infra-bot: Incident reminder: gpu-pool-7 memory alert triggered at 2025-11-21T09:12:02Z. Pager duty: @oncall-eng.
sasha: For short-term: deploy patch that enforces per-tenant hard reserve (e.g., 1GB) + per-tenant soft cap at 10GB with aging window = 10m. That will prevent single tenant from getting >10GB.
ajay: I can sketch the rollout: 1) add per-tenant metrics (easy) 2) soft TTL + aging eviction 3) fairness boost 4) allocator compaction fix. Rollout in canary then pool-wide.
maria: For the allocator compaction, here's the failing snippet from the run: 
```
# allocator stats
free_chunks_small: 14k
fragmentation_ratio: 0.42
compaction_runs: 0 (expected >0)
```
devon: Timeline? I can own steps 1-2 this week, maria can take 4, ajay do 3 and rollout plan. Sasha can review and own canary gating.
sasha: Sounds good. Also add a perf test that simulates 1000 unique long contexts to validate reuse hits and resident growth. We need automated regression checks.
ajay: Agreed. Also let's add an smoke test: create micro-tenant that repeatedly opens long contexts but low qps — ensure we reclaim after TTL.
maria: One more thought: consider compact-on-evict: when evicting we try to coalesce freed chunks immediately if fragmentation ratio > 0.3. That might reduce future memory growth.
devon: Will log experimental configs and results in the perf-runner channel. Planning to run 3 variants: baseline, soft-ttl-only, soft-ttl+fairness.
sasha: Assigning owners in the thread: devon (soft-ttl + metrics), maria (allocator compaction), ajay (fairness + rollout). I'll create a follow-up GH issue for tracking. :thumbsup:
ajay: Thanks — putting PR draft up later today. Will tag @sasha @maria for review.
